summary: Regression of an enzyme's Michaelis constant (Km) for a substrate, from the protein sequence and substrate SMILES.
what_it_measures: log10(Km) in M for an enzyme–substrate pair, standardized (`km_standardized`); the substrate concentration at half-maximal rate, i.e. apparent substrate affinity. A protein+ligand task.
assay_method: In-vitro steady-state kinetics compiled and cleaned by CatPred, with de-duplication and sequence-identity-aware evaluation splits.
provenance: From the CatPred Km benchmark; substrate SMILES are canonicalized and described by the 200 normalized RDKit 2D descriptors of descriptastorus (RDKit2DNormalized), concatenated with the protein embedding.
when_to_use: Complements kcat: tests whether representations capture substrate-binding affinity. Useful when ranking models for enzyme–substrate specificity prediction.
caveats: Km is noisy and assay-dependent; log10 targets standardized on the training split (MAE in standardized units). Much of the signal comes from the substrate descriptors: the no-PLM baseline comes within 0.04 of the best PLM here.

citations.authors: Boorla, V. S. & Maranas, C. D.
citations.title: CatPred: a comprehensive framework for deep learning in vitro enzyme kinetic parameters
